matchup: Hawaii Rainbow Warriors @ Stanford Cardinal
rationale: Stanford's starting quarterback has not played in a game in nearly 20 months. Davis Warren tore his right ACL in the ReliaQuest Bowl to end the 2024 season, sat out all of 2025, and was named the starter only in the final week of camp, in front of a head coach working his first game and two new coordinators. Hawai'i brings back Micah Alejado, who threw for 3,106 yards and 24 touchdowns last season, and a staff in its fifth year, so the side with the settled quarterback is the one getting points. The number opened at 5.5, traded to 3.5 on Wednesday and sits at 4.5 today, so this is the best price available since the move. I am wrong if Warren plays like the quarterback who started nine games for Michigan in 2024, and the risk is on my own side too, because Hawai'i has to replace 17 starters and the model only likes this by 1.9 points.

sources.quote: It has been nearly 20 months since Warren played in a game.

sources.claim: The main argument against this pick, that Hawai'i has almost no returning production outside quarterback.
sources.quote: UH will have to replace 17 starters across offense, defense and special teams.

matchup: NC State Wolfpack @ Virginia Cavaliers
rationale: Virginia's first ACC availability report of the season lists 16 players out, and four of them are wide receivers, including Rico Flores, the projected top target, who spent training camp on a hamstring. The same report takes out the placekicker, which is worth real points in a game the market prices inside five, and NC State comes the other way returning CJ Bailey. make_slate found no candidate here, so the ratings model agrees with the market inside 1.5 points and this pick rests entirely on the report. Against that, the number has already moved from 5.5 to 4.5 and the moneyline from 220 to 178 since Wednesday, and the hook costs 115, so most of the news is in the price. I am wrong if that point the market already gave back was the whole edge and Virginia's remaining receivers hold up.

sources.quote: Wednesday's initial ACC weekly injury report listed 16 Cavaliers as out against the Wolfpack.

sources.quote: Most notable is Flores, a transfer from UCLA, who dealt with hamstring issues during training camp.

sources.claim: NC State returns its starting quarterback.
sources.quote: NC State's roster has also gone through many changes, but they return one of the ACC's best quarterbacks in CJ Bailey.

matchup: Memphis Tigers @ UNLV Rebels
rationale: Memphis has not named a starting quarterback three days before its first game under a first year head coach, with two transfers still splitting the job, while UNLV named Jackson Arnold and kept Dan Mullen and most of its staff. The model likes UNLV by 1.7 points and the number has come from 5.5 to 4.5, so the price is better than it was a week ago. What stops this from going live is that the move is money on Memphis rather than a stale line, and UNLV's own game notes say the Rebels return seven starters, so the continuity argument is thinner than it reads from the outside. I am wrong if Memphis settles on a quarterback who plays well immediately, which is exactly what the market appears to be betting on.

sources.claim: UNLV's continuity is weaker than the narrative suggests, with seven returning starters.
sources.quote: The Rebels return 32 lettermen (12 O/19 D/1 ST) and seven starters (3 on each side of the ball plus a PK).

matchup: Memphis Tigers @ UNLV Rebels
rationale: This is the largest gap on the board, 10.3 points, with the model at 66.8 against a market of 56.5 in a dome where weather cannot take a game under. UNLV's defense finished 89th nationally last season and the projection has both teams above 30 points. The reason it stays a shadow pick is that the total has moved down from 57.5 rather than up, and Memphis has no settled quarterback under a new staff, which is the ordinary way an opener stalls in the first quarter. I am wrong about calling it off if both offenses come out clean and the number was simply slow to catch up to two 30 point projections.

matchup: North Carolina Tar Heels @ TCU Horned Frogs
rationale: The ratings model has this at 4.9 on a neutral field in Dublin and the market has moved the other way, from 7.5 to 8.5 with the moneyline going 330 to 360, which is the market telling me the carryover ratings are stale. Search results describe North Carolina arriving without its defensive coordinator, who is on medical leave, and without its general manager, who is on administrative leave, but I could not open those pages to confirm the wording, so I am not treating either as established and I am keeping this well below the publish line. A second year program that turned over most of its roster is exactly where last season's numbers lie to you. I am wrong if the 3.6 points the model sees are real and the off field news is noise, which is the case for taking the points here.

matchup: San Jose State Spartans @ USC Trojans
rationale: The model wants 35.4 and the market is laying 38.5, so there are 3.1 points here, and San Jose State starts an experienced quarterback in Luke Weaver rather than the walk on a number this size usually implies. Numbers above four touchdowns are also where a favourite's own clock management does the covering, and USC has no reason to chase points in the fourth quarter of an opener. What keeps it a shadow pick is that I found no researched reason the market is wrong, only the rating gap, and the gap alone is what the 7.5 cap exists to refuse. I am wrong if USC treats this as a statement game and the reserves keep scoring.

matchup: Sacramento State Hornets @ Eastern Michigan Eagles
rationale: The model likes the points by 4.1 and the number has not moved off 9.5 in nine days, which normally means nobody has an opinion worth acting on. The research argues the other way, because Sacramento State is playing its first game as an FBS program, under a first year head coach, 2,300 miles from home, and a rating built on last season's FCS schedule is the least reliable number the model produces. That is a case for fading my own model rather than following it, and I am not confident enough in either direction to do more than log it. I am wrong about the caution if Sacramento State's roster travelled better than a reclassifying program usually does.

matchup: Jacksonville State Gamecocks @ North Dakota State Bison
rationale: The model has this 9.5 points over the market, which would be the second largest edge on the board, and the Fargodome removes weather from the question. Against that, North Dakota State is replacing both its starting quarterback and its lead running back in its first FBS season, and a 46.5 total between two teams that won at this level by playing defence and shortening games looks like the market pricing something the ratings cannot see. I am logging the model's side at 6.0 rather than taking it, because I think the honest read here is the Under and I do not have the research to bet against my own projection either. I am wrong if North Dakota State's new backfield is as productive as the one it replaced.

matchup: New Mexico State Aggies @ Florida State Seminoles
rationale: Three points of model edge on the points, and Florida State is breaking in a new starting quarterback in Ashton Daniels, which is the usual way a heavy favourite stalls for a quarter and never gets the number back. The 115 price on a 32.5 hook eats most of a three point edge, and I found nothing researched that says the market is wrong, so this stays a shadow pick. Florida State reported no injuries to key players, which removes the one angle that would have moved it. I am wrong if Daniels is comfortable immediately and Florida State scores into the fourth quarter.

matchup: Wyoming Cowboys @ Colorado State Rams
rationale: Neither team has a quarterback the other has seen. Colorado State is in year one under Jim Mora, who has kept the job open between transfers Hauss Hejny and K'saan Farrar since March and has said the decision does not have to be made until kickoff, and Wyoming answers with Tyler Hughes, who arrived from William and Mary in January and has never taken an FBS snap. The blended ratings put this game at 35.2 points against a market number of 46.5, the second largest total gap on the board, and both offenses grade in the mid teens while both defenses return more of their work. I am paying -118 on a number that already fell from 47.5 to 46.5, so the cheap side of this move is gone and I am agreeing with money rather than beating it, which is what holds this at 8.0 instead of higher. Hughes ran for 670 yards at William and Mary, and a mobile quarterback who plays clean in his first FBS start is the version of this game that goes over.

matchup: Clemson Tigers @ LSU Tigers
rationale: Clemson starts Christopher Vizzina, whose only meaningful college sample is one home loss to SMU last October, and he opens on the road at night in Tiger Stadium against an SEC defense. LSU is rebuilding around Lane Kiffin in his first game there with over half the roster new, so both offenses are less settled than either defense. The model says 40.9 against a market number of 50.5. What keeps this off the card is that Sam Leavitt is an established starter rather than an unknown and Kiffin offenses score at a high rate, so the LSU half of the under argument is much weaker than the Clemson half, and 50.5 is not a high number for two ranked teams. I am wrong if Leavitt is comfortable early and LSU turns the Clemson quarterback over into short fields.

sources.claim: Clemson's starting quarterback has one meaningful game of college experience.
sources.quote: Vizzina's only sample size comes from a home loss to SMU back in October, throwing for 317 yards and three touchdowns.

sources.quote: That'll be a challenge, especially with the emotions of this game and the first game in the stadium and at night, so we'll talk extensively about that throughout the week.

matchup: East Carolina Pirates @ Alabama Crimson Tide
rationale: Alabama hands the offense to Keelon Russell for his first career start behind a run game that finished 125th nationally last season, and East Carolina arrives having replaced most of a 9-4 roster. The model reads the total at 43.4 against a market number of 52.5. I could not open the preview carrying East Carolina's returning production figure, so I am not citing it and I am not rating this on it. The reason this stays a shadow rather than a play is that a five star making a first start at home against a Group of Five defense is the softest possible landing spot, and Alabama alone can reach 40. I am wrong if Russell is efficient early and Alabama scores on its first four possessions.

matchup: Akron Zips @ Wake Forest Demon Deacons
rationale: Wake Forest opens with Gio Lopez, a first year starter after transferring from North Carolina, and Akron's intended starter Reese Poffenbarger carries an unresolved eligibility question that may leave Braydon Roggow taking the snaps on a Thursday night. The model reads this total at 38.8 against a market number of 48.5. I did not open a page confirming the eligibility situation, so that claim is unconfirmed and the rating reflects that rather than assuming it. Two unproven quarterbacks in an opener is the same argument I am already making elsewhere on this card, which is a further reason to leave it as a shadow. I am wrong if Wake Forest scores at will against a Mid American defense and the game is decided by halftime.

matchup: Marshall Thundering Herd @ Penn State Nittany Lions
rationale: This is the largest total gap on the board at 12.3 points, with the model at 64.8 against a market number of 52.5, and unlike most of the board the research does not cut against it. Penn State starts Rocco Becht, who made 39 starts at Iowa State, and Marshall returns Carlos Del Rio-Wilson, the Sun Belt preseason offensive player of the year who ran for 660 yards last season. What holds it down is that Matt Campbell is in his first game at Penn State and new staffs open conservatively, and a 24.5 point favorite that leads comfortably will shorten the second half. I am wrong if Penn State empties the bench up 28 and the fourth quarter is a running clock.

matchup: Florida International Panthers @ South Florida Bulls
rationale: The model reads this total at 63.1 against a market number of 51.5, an 11.6 point gap that survives the calibration adjustment. I did no research on either roster beyond the ratings, so this is logged as a pure model candidate and rated accordingly rather than talked up to the card. It is here because the grader needs the model's raw total edges tracked to find out whether they are worth anything, and September totals off carryover ratings are exactly the cell with no data in it. I am wrong if either offense is worse than last season's rating, which is the common case for a model running on carryover numbers.

matchup: Coastal Carolina Chanticleers @ West Virginia Mountaineers
rationale: West Virginia's own staff said on Wednesday that this roster has not played together, with Rich Rodriguez calling himself anxious because so many of his players have not run this system and defensive coordinator Zac Alley saying his worry is nerves rather than talent. A team laying 21.5 points has to execute cleanly for four quarters, and a portal-built roster in its first game together is the least likely version of West Virginia to do that. The ratings make this a 15.6 point game, so the market is asking for nearly a touchdown more than the projection and asking a brand new offense to deliver it at noon. What beats me is Coastal's quarterback: Thad Hudson left for N.C. State and the likely starter has 47 career pass attempts, so if the Chanticleers cannot move the ball at all the number stops mattering.

matchup: Liberty Flames @ James Madison Dukes
rationale: The consensus total on this game is 52.5 and FanDuel is at 50.5, so the Over is available 2 points below where the rest of the market has it. James Madison turned over most of the roster that reached the playoff and is leaning on transfers to carry a new offense, which is the profile of a team that scores in bursts and gives up more than its rating suggests while everything is still being installed. Liberty's defensive front is experienced but undersized, and the projection has this game at 60 points against a market number in the low 50s. The mechanism that beats me is the new coordinator's run game, because an offense that ripped teams apart on the ground also shortens the game and takes possessions off the board.

sources.claim: James Madison is relying almost entirely on transfers while Liberty returns its own veterans
sources.quote: Liberty is a team full of its own veterans with a few transfers sprinkled in, and James Madison will be almost fully reliant on the transfers to shine right away.

sources.claim: Liberty's defensive front is not big or talented enough to hold down the new James Madison offense
sources.quote: The Liberty defensive front is experienced, but it's not all that big and not quite talented enough to handle what the new-look JMU offense is about to bring.

matchup: East Carolina Pirates @ Alabama Crimson Tide
rationale: Alabama is handing its offense to Keelon Russell, who won the job in camp and has almost no game experience, and asking him to cover 27.5 points in a 12 p.m. kickoff in his first start. East Carolina is not a typical guarantee-game opponent either, with a defense described as good enough to be a problem and a portal-rebuilt offense that should move the ball. The ratings make this a 22.8 point game, so the market is charging nearly 5 points more than the projection for a team whose passing game has never taken a live snap together. The way this goes wrong is the Alabama defense simply ending it early, which is the explicit expectation even if the offense is slow to start.

sources.claim: East Carolina's defense and rebuilt offense make it a live underdog rather than a walkover
sources.quote: The defense is good enough to be a problem, and all the new parts from the transfer portal should keep things going on the offensive side.

matchup: UCLA Bruins @ California Golden Bears
rationale: California returns the better quarterback in this game by a wide margin, with Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele having thrown for over 3,400 yards as a true freshman while Nico Iamaleava managed 1,938 yards with 13 touchdowns and 7 interceptions in his first year at UCLA. The ratings make Cal a 1.2 point favorite at home and the market has the Bears taking 1.5, so this is a free crossing of the pick-em line in the direction the projection already points. A 10:30 p.m. Eastern kickoff in Berkeley is also the kind of environment that flattens a visiting team more than a flat 2.2 point home field number allows. The honest counterweight is that the local beat writers all picked UCLA by three or four, so I am on the opposite side of the people who watch this team every day.

sources.claim: Cal's quarterback threw for more than 3,400 yards as a true freshman and is the harder matchup
sources.quote: Containing a quarterback who threw for over 3,400 yards in his true freshman campaign will be no small task.

matchup: Marshall Thundering Herd @ Penn State Nittany Lions
rationale: This is the one game on the card where I am taking the opposite side of the ratings model, which projects 64.8 points and is running on last year's Penn State, not Matt Campbell's. Campbell brought Rocco Becht and a load of former Cyclones with him, and the described plan is a balanced offense without many crazy ideas, which is a description of a team that runs the ball with a big lead rather than one that hangs 45. Marshall has a capable quarterback in Carlos Del Rio-Wilson but is a 24.5 point underdog, so the realistic path to 53 points requires Penn State to keep throwing late. If Campbell decides his new offense needs the live reps and leaves the starters in, this goes over without much drama.

sources.claim: Penn State's new offense under Matt Campbell is expected to be balanced and conservative

sources.quote: Marshall has a good quarterback in Carlos Del Rio-Wilson, who showed last year what he could do when getting time to work.

matchup: Oregon State Beavers @ Houston Cougars
rationale: The ratings like Oregon State getting 20.5 and make this a 16.4 point game, but the research runs the other way hard enough that I am rating this below the rest of the card rather than trusting the gap. Oregon State is 3-16 over its last 19 games and did not win a road game last season, while Houston went 10-3 and won all six of its road games. The 4 point disagreement is real but it is built on carryover ratings that still have some 2024 Oregon State in them. I am keeping this on the board because the number is genuinely large and Houston has to prove the offense travels to a noon kickoff, but I would not defend it above a 7.

sources.quote: Oregon State is just 3-16 over its last 19 games.
